::: {#def-feedforward-network}

#### Feedforward network (multilayer perceptron, MLP)

A **feedforward network**, or **multilayer perceptron** (**MLP**),
computes its output $\vecf{\hy}$ from its input $\vx$
through a sequence of $K$ [hidden layers](#def-hidden-layer),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vhidval^{(1)} &= g\paren{\matr{W}^{(1)} \vx + \vecf{b}^{(1)}}, \\
\vhidval^{(\layeridx)} &= g\paren{\matr{W}^{(\layeridx)} \vhidval^{(\layeridx - 1)} + \vecf{b}^{(\layeridx)}},
\qquad \layeridx = 2, \dots, K, \\
\vecf{\hy} &= \matr{W}^{(K + 1)} \vhidval^{(K)} + \vecf{b}^{(K + 1)},
\end{aligned}
$$

where $g$ is an [activation function](#def-activation-function) and the weight matrices $\matr{W}^{(\layeridx)}$ and bias vectors $\vecf{b}^{(\layeridx)}$ are its [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter)
[@goodfellow2016deep, Ch. 6].
Information flows from the input to the output, with no path from a later layer back to an earlier one;
"feedforward" names that.

Every layer of an MLP is [fully connected](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-fully-connected),
so it is also called a fully connected network,
and *Deep Learning* calls it a deep feedforward network. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
It contains no perceptron in Rosenblatt's sense, a threshold function of a weighted sum [@rosenblatt1958perceptron],
so the name is historical.
Its [depth](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-depth) is $K + 1$.
The last layer has no activation function;
how its numbers become predictions depends on the task.

:::
